links.outcome: Patient-reported graft-loss treatment conversations and SDM outcomes versus usual care
links.effect: Despite AUC-ROC 0.923, conversations did not differ: intervention 14/36 (39%) vs control 16/40 (40%), p = 1.00; no differences in secondary clinical, SDM, relationship, or distress outcomes.
links.quote: Passive EHR availability of AI risk estimates did not improve communication or SDM-related outcomes.

links.outcome: Clinician tool utilization and barriers to use
links.effect: Mean reported utilization 29% (SD 37%); one physician 100%, others 0–30%. Barriers included separate EHR tab without direct workflow integration and no alerts for high-risk scores.
links.quote: Users described the following reasons as main barriers to use the system: lack of immediate clinical consequence or no perceived need for risk stratification, lack of time during the visit, no direct integration into workflow since the integration was provided in another tab of the EHR, no alerts in case of high-risk scores.

models_evaluated: Gradient-boosted regression tree model predicting 360-day death-censored graft failure

links.outcome: Treatment-option conversations and secondary clinical outcomes with AI-supported care versus usual care
links.effect: Despite AUC-ROC 0.923, conversations were intervention 14/36 [39%] vs control 16/40 [40%]; chi-square p = 1.00. No significant between-group differences occurred in secondary clinical outcomes.
links.quote: Conversation frequency did not differ between groups (intervention 14/36 [39%] vs control 16/40 [40%]; chi-square p = 1.00).

links.outcome: Clinician-reported tool utilization and workflow barriers
links.effect: Utilization averaged 29%, SD 37%; one physician reported 100%, remaining physicians 0–30%. Reported barriers included time constraints, a separate EHR tab, absent high-risk alerts, and no perceived clinical consequence.
links.quote: The reported utilization differed highly between physicians (one physician reported 100% utilization, while all remaining physicians reported 0–30%; mean 29%, SD 37%), precluding meaningful stratified analysis by clinician-level uptake.

links.effect: Conversation frequency did not differ between the intervention and control groups (39% vs 40%).
links.quote: Conversation frequency did not differ between groups (intervention 14/36 [39%] vs control 16/40 [40%]; chi-square p = 1.00).

links.effect: Clinicians reported a lack of immediate clinical consequence for the risk stratification as a main barrier to using the system.
links.quote: Users described the following reasons as main barriers to use the system: lack of immediate clinical consequence or no perceived need for risk stratification, lack of time during the visit, no direct integration into workflow since the integration was provided in another tab of the EHR, no alerts in case of high-risk scores.

links.effect: The lack of direct workflow integration, requiring navigation to another EHR tab, was reported as a main barrier to system use.
links.quote: Users described the following reasons as main barriers to use the system: lack of immediate clinical consequence or no perceived need for risk stratification, lack of time during the visit, no direct integration into workflow since the integration was provided in another tab of the EHR, no alerts in case of high-risk scores.

links.effect: Suboptimal workflow integration and perceived limited utility in routine visits resulted in limited use of the AI risk information.
links.quote: The post-study user survey indicated limited use of the AI risk information, with barriers including time constraints, perceived limited utility in routine visits, and suboptimal workflow integration (e.g., requiring navigation rather than appearing in-context or via alerts).
